hero.headline: US Restricts Foreign Access to Anthropic's Latest AI Models
hero.body:
The US government has ordered Anthropic to suspend access to its most advanced AI models, Fable 5 and Mythos 5, for all foreign nationals, citing national security concerns. The company received an export control directive without being given specific details about the security issues involved.

Anthropic announced it will "abruptly disable" these models for all users in response to the government order. The restrictions mark a significant shift in how the US regulates access to cutting-edge artificial intelligence technology, applying export controls typically reserved for physical hardware to AI systems themselves.

The move comes after Anthropic disclosed that unauthorised users gained access to its Mythos model through a third-party vendor environment. Bloomberg reported that a small group of people in a private online forum accessed the model on the same day Anthropic began releasing it to select companies including Apple and Goldman Sachs for testing. One of the unauthorised users worked as a contractor for Anthropic and deployed methods used by cybersecurity researchers to gain access. According to Bloomberg, the group was primarily interested in "playing around" with the technology rather than causing harm, and had not run cybersecurity tests on the model.

The incident raised alarms among government authorities who have expressed serious concerns about Mythos's capabilities. The UK's AI Security Institute warned that Mythos represents a "step up" from previous models in terms of cyber-threat potential. The model can identify software vulnerabilities and conduct attacks requiring multiple actions without human intervention, tasks that would normally take human professionals days to complete. Mythos successfully completed a 32-step cyber-attack simulation created by the security institute in three of ten attempts.

Kanishka Narayan, the UK's AI minister, cautioned that UK businesses "should be worried" about the model's ability to detect flaws in IT systems that hackers could exploit.

Anthropic's CEO stated that research leading to the US export restrictions was conducted for defense and cybersecurity purposes. The CEO emphasised that the work was not a jailbreak of the AI systems but rather legitimate security testing.

The government's decision to impose export controls on AI model access rather than just underlying hardware represents a new approach to technology regulation. As AI companies continue developing increasingly capable systems, US officials are taking a more proactive stance on controlling access to advanced tools. The restrictions aim to maintain American advantages in AI development while preventing potential adversaries from accessing systems that could be used for military or intelligence purposes.

The move could set a precedent for how other leading AI systems are regulated in the future as national security concerns around advanced AI capabilities intensify.

cards.headline: US and Iran expected to sign peace framework Sunday
cards.teaser: President Trump said the US and Iran plan to sign an agreement aimed at ending their conflict and easing nuclear tensions.
cards.body:
President Trump announced on Saturday that the US and Iran plan to sign a peace agreement on Sunday. According to Trump's post on Truth Social, the deal would prevent Iran from obtaining nuclear weapons and reopen the Strait of Hormuz to international shipping.

However, Iran cast doubt on the timeline, stating that an exact signing date has not been decided and that it "will not be tomorrow." Democratic Rep. Seth Moulton of Massachusetts criticized the reported terms, calling the agreement a surrender document.

cards.headline: Tren de Aragua Gang Leader Killed in Joint US-Venezuela Strike
cards.teaser: A Venezuelan gang leader wanted in the United States was killed in a joint military operation this week.
cards.body:
Hector Rusthenford Guerrero Flores, known as Niño Guerrero, was killed in a military strike in Venezuela this week. President Trump announced the operation, describing it as a "swift and lethal kinetic strike" carried out by US Southern Command with Venezuelan assistance.

Niño Guerrero was a leader of Tren de Aragua, a Venezuelan street gang that Trump characterized as a terrorist organization. The operation represents a rare instance of cooperation between the United States and Venezuela, whose governments have maintained strained relations for years.

cards.headline: Pentagon Adds Alibaba, Baidu and BYD to Chinese Military Company List
cards.teaser: The Pentagon has designated three of China's largest technology companies as supporters of the Chinese military, drawing sharp criticism from Beijing.
cards.body:
The Pentagon has added Alibaba, Baidu, and BYD to its list of Chinese companies deemed to support Beijing's military. The update, released Monday, supersedes an earlier 2025 list and targets major firms across e-commerce, search, and electric vehicle manufacturing.

The timing is significant, coming less than a month after Donald Trump visited Beijing and met with Xi Jinping to maintain a trade war truce. China's government expressed strong dissatisfaction with the Pentagon's decision, calling it a move that could inflame bilateral tensions. The designations can restrict American companies from conducting business with the listed Chinese firms.

cards.headline: State attorneys general open investigation into OpenAI
cards.body:
Multiple state attorneys general have launched an investigation into OpenAI, examining a range of practices at the artificial intelligence company. The inquiry covers topics including how OpenAI handles advertising policies and its management of health data, according to reports.

The investigation represents a new front of regulatory scrutiny for OpenAI, which has faced increasing attention from government officials as its AI products have gained widespread use. The company's ChatGPT chatbot and other tools have raised questions about data privacy, content moderation, and consumer protection across various jurisdictions.

Which states are participating in the investigation has not been disclosed. State-level enforcement actions have become an increasingly common avenue for technology regulation in the United States, particularly when federal agencies have not moved quickly on emerging issues. Attorneys general from multiple states often coordinate investigations into technology companies, sharing resources and information.

The scope of the inquiry appears broad, touching on both commercial practices around advertising and sensitive matters involving health information. How AI companies collect, store, and use health data has emerged as a particular concern among regulators, given the sensitive nature of medical information and the potential for AI systems to process such data in ways users may not fully understand.

OpenAI has faced other regulatory challenges in recent months as governments worldwide grapple with how to oversee rapidly advancing AI technology. The company has emphasized its commitment to safety and responsible development, but questions persist about transparency, data handling, and the potential impacts of its systems. The state investigation adds to a growing list of oversight efforts that could shape how OpenAI and other AI companies operate going forward.

cards.headline: Justice Department Approves Paramount Acquisition of Warner Bros.
cards.teaser: The Justice Department has cleared the way for Paramount to purchase Warner Bros., approving one of the largest media mergers in recent years.
cards.body:
The Department of Justice has approved the $111 billion merger between Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros. Discovery, clearing a significant regulatory milestone for the deal. The acquisition will combine two major entertainment conglomerates with extensive film libraries, television networks, and streaming platforms.

The approval comes after months of antitrust review, despite industry concerns about reduced competition. The merger will bring together Paramount's CBS News with Warner Bros. Discovery's CNN and HBO. The deal still faces scrutiny from UK regulators and potential legal challenges from state attorneys general.

cards.headline: New Student Loan Plan Raises Payments for Many Borrowers
cards.teaser: Changes to student loan repayment programs will result in higher monthly bills for many borrowers starting next month.
cards.body:
A new student loan repayment plan will increase monthly payments for many borrowers, with major changes taking effect July 1. The shift follows the repeal of the SAVE program, leaving some borrowers with hundreds of thousands of dollars in debt facing uncertainty about their repayment options.

Tax planning strategies may help some borrowers reduce their payments under the new system, according to financial advisors. Graduates from the class of 2026 are being advised against consolidating their loans as the new rules take effect. The changes represent a significant shift in how federal student loan repayment is structured.

hero.headline: Trump Announces US-Iran Deal Signing for Sunday as Tehran Questions Timeline
hero.body:
President Trump announced on Saturday that a peace agreement with Iran would be signed the following day, claiming the deal would prevent Tehran from obtaining a nuclear weapon and reopen the strait of Hormuz to international shipping. However, Iranian officials quickly disputed the timeline, with Tehran's foreign ministry saying no final decision had been made on when a signing would occur.

In a post on Truth Social, Trump stated that Iran "no longer want a Nuclear Weapon, nor will they have one, either through purchase, development, or any other form of procurement." He added that the Hormuz Strait would open immediately after signing and that the US relationship with Iran under his administration would be "much different and better" than under previous presidents.

Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif said on Saturday that Islamabad was preparing for an electronic signing within 24 hours, followed by technical-level talks the following week. He expressed confidence that the deal would form a foundation for lasting peace in the region.

Esmaeil Baghaei, Iran's foreign ministry spokesperson, took a more cautious approach. He said an exact signing date had not been determined and that a signing would not happen on Sunday. He suggested the possibility of a signing occurring in the coming days but made no firm commitment.

The conflicting statements reflected deeper disagreements between the sides over the deal's substance and implementation. US officials claimed the agreement would result in the destruction of Iran's enriched uranium and dismantling of its nuclear program, with no frozen assets released until Iran met certain conditions. Iran's version, according to reports from its semi-official news agency, described a different outcome, including the release of 24 billion dollars in frozen assets and only a 60-day period for nuclear negotiations.

The proposed deal also outlined different understandings on regional security. According to Iranian sources, the agreement would address conflicts across multiple fronts, including Lebanon, where Israel has conducted operations against Hezbollah. The deal would suspend sanctions on Iran's oil sales, allow Iran to charge for passage through the strait of Hormuz, and lift the US naval blockade on Iranian ports.

Trump has previously claimed numerous times that a deal was imminent, only to revert to threats of military action against Iran. Recent weeks have seen intense clashes between Iran and Israel, with the conflict disrupting critical shipping routes and threatening global energy supplies.

Both sides are attempting to frame a potential agreement as a victory to their respective domestic audiences. Iran's foreign minister stated that his country had emerged stronger from the conflict, while US officials said the deal met Trump's core objectives. The coming days will determine whether the two sides can overcome their differences and finalize an agreement.

cards.headline: Ukrainian Drone Strike Kills One in Southern Russia, Triggers Fire at Sea Terminal
cards.teaser: A Ukrainian drone attack killed one person in southern Russia and sparked a fire at a sea terminal.
cards.body:
Ukrainian forces struck a sea terminal in Russia's Volgograd region, killing one person and causing a fire, according to Russian authorities. The attack targeted energy infrastructure as part of Ukraine's broader campaign against Russian oil and gas facilities.

Ukraine has escalated strikes on Russian energy infrastructure in recent months, with military officials in Kyiv stating they will continue targeting energy assets to disrupt fuel supplies supporting Russian military operations.

cards.headline: Top Haitian Security Official Kidnapped Amid Spreading Violence
cards.teaser: A security expert who recently became chief of staff to Haiti's new defense minister was abducted.
cards.body:
The chief of staff to Haiti's new defense minister was kidnapped in the latest incident of violence affecting the country. The official, described as a security expert, had only recently taken the position under the new defense minister.

The abduction underscores the deteriorating security situation in Haiti, where kidnappings have become increasingly common. Armed groups have expanded their control over parts of the capital and other areas, targeting government officials, business leaders, and ordinary citizens for ransom.

cards.headline: Tren de Aragua Gang Leader Killed in Joint US-Venezuela Strike
cards.teaser: A Venezuelan gang leader wanted in the United States was killed in a joint military operation this week.
cards.body:
Hector Rusthenford Guerrero Flores, known as Niño Guerrero, was killed in a military strike in Venezuela this week. President Trump announced the operation, describing it as a "swift and lethal kinetic strike" carried out by US Southern Command with Venezuelan assistance.

cards.headline: Five Children Killed in Vehicle Collision in Rural Ontario
cards.teaser: Four girls and one boy died when a van and SUV collided in rural Ontario.
cards.body:
Five children were killed when a van carrying 10 people collided with an SUV in rural Ontario. The victims included four girls and one boy. An infant in the van was seriously injured in the crash, police said.

Authorities did not release information about the cause of the collision or the conditions of other passengers. The crash occurred in a rural area of the province.

cards.headline: Canadian Prime Minister Calls for Canada-EU Unity Before G7 Summit
cards.teaser: Mark Carney urged closer cooperation between Canada and European nations ahead of the upcoming G7 meeting.
cards.body:
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney arrived in Dublin for a two-day visit to Ireland, where he met with Taoiseach Micheál Martin. Carney called for greater unity between Canada and European Union members ahead of the G7 summit, describing the need as a response to what he termed "a global rupture" affecting international cooperation.

The G7 summit will convene leaders from Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, France, Germany, Italy, and Japan. Carney's remarks indicate he intends to emphasize strengthened transatlantic coordination during the meetings.

cards.headline: Iran's Leadership Shows Greater Willingness to Resist US Pressure
cards.teaser: Iran's new government has demonstrated increased confidence in withstanding American and Israeli military and economic threats.
cards.body:
Iran's new, more militaristic leaders have already survived significant military and economic pressure from the United States and Israel, and appear readier to take risks in negotiations. This shift reflects their assessment that they can endure ongoing sanctions and threats while pursuing their regional goals.

The change in Iran's approach has affected diplomatic efforts between Washington and Tehran. As negotiations continue, Iranian officials have adopted harder negotiating positions compared to earlier rounds of talks, complicating efforts to reach agreement.

hero.headline: Trump's name removed from Kennedy Center amid legal dispute
hero.body:
Donald Trump's name has been removed from the facade of the Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts in Washington, D.C., following a federal judge's decision to reject an emergency appeal seeking to block the removal.

The work began in the early hours of Saturday, shortly after the performing arts venue missed a federal judge's two-week deadline to remove the words "The Donald J Trump and" from the building's exterior by Friday at 11:59 p.m. local time.

On Friday evening, an appeals court in Washington D.C. rejected an emergency appeal filed by the Justice Department on behalf of Trump and his hand-picked Kennedy Center board members. The appeal sought to pause U.S. District Judge Christopher Cooper's order mandating the removal of Trump's name from the building. Earlier that same day, Cooper had denied a last-minute bid by the Kennedy Center to keep his name on the facade.

Crowds gathered at the Kennedy Center on Friday night as workers assembled scaffolding along the building, which had been formally named the Donald J Trump and the John F Kennedy Memorial Center for the Performing Arts. Onlookers cheered workers in hard hats and yellow vests as they prepared to remove the president's name from the marbled exterior, with some chanting "Take it down!"

Many Washington residents have viewed the rebranding of the Kennedy Center as problematic. Carolyn, a 50-year-old retired government worker, expressed her perspective on the naming situation, saying: "Putting his name on everything is right out of the dictator playbook." This sentiment reflects broader concerns among capital residents who see Trump's architectural ambitions as narcissistic and anti-democratic.

The Kennedy Center serves as the national cultural center of the United States and operates as a living memorial to President John F. Kennedy. As a federally funded institution, the center hosts theater, dance, music performances, and other cultural events. The legal dispute over the display of Trump's name raised questions about the appropriate use of naming rights at federal institutions.

The removal represents a significant moment in the relationship between the Trump name and federal properties. Work to remove the signage continued beyond Friday, with storms initially delaying the removal until Saturday morning. A covering remains in place at the location where Trump's name previously appeared on the building while the Kennedy Center determines what permanent signage, if any, will replace it.

The situation highlights the intersection of politics and cultural institutions, drawing attention to how federal agencies and publicly funded organizations address naming disputes involving controversial figures.

cards.headline: Trump appoints James McDonald to lead Manhattan federal prosecutors office
cards.teaser: President Trump has selected James M. McDonald to head the powerful Southern District of New York federal prosecutors office.
cards.body:
President Trump has named James M. McDonald to lead the United States Attorney's Office for the Southern District of New York. McDonald is a partner at Sullivan & Cromwell and previously worked as an enforcer at the Commodity Futures Trading Commission. He served on Trump's defense team.

The Southern District of New York oversees high-profile cases involving financial crimes, corruption, and national security matters in Manhattan and surrounding areas. The office is known for its independent investigations and has prosecuted major cases involving Wall Street firms, organized crime, and public officials.

cards.headline: Pentagon releases new UFO files including reports of glowing orbs
cards.teaser: The White House has released a third batch of unidentified flying object files through a new Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System.
cards.body:
The Department of War has released new unidentified aerial phenomena records through the Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters, known as PURSUE. The files include reports of glowing red orbs and other mysterious sightings. One report from Colorado describes an object resembling a potato hovering in the sky.

The release includes video footage of mysterious orbs and detailed accounts from witnesses who reported unusual aerial activity. Multiple sightings involved glowing objects that displayed flight characteristics not typical of known aircraft. The files represent the third batch of UFO records made public by the Pentagon as part of increased transparency efforts regarding unexplained aerial phenomena.

cards.headline: Texas Republicans adopt platform including IVF and Sharia law restrictions
cards.teaser: The Texas Republican Party has added new provisions to its platform at the state convention in Houston.
cards.body:
Texas Republicans have expanded their party platform to include bans on in vitro fertilization and Sharia law. The changes were adopted at the Republican state convention in Houston, where Governor Greg Abbott outlined his vision for a fourth term. The platform reflects an increasingly conservative direction for the state party.

The convention also featured the election of new party leadership. Abraham George, the first Indian-American chairperson of the Texas GOP, lost his re-election bid. The gathering drew reactions to various policy positions as Texas Republicans assembled to set their agenda ahead of upcoming elections.

cards.headline: Live elephant brought to Texas GOP convention urinates on floor
cards.teaser: An elephant wearing a banner with Governor Abbott's name urinated during the Texas Republican Party convention in Houston.
cards.body:
The Texas Republican Party brought a 4-ton African elephant named Paige to its state convention in Houston as a surprise for attendees following Governor Greg Abbott's keynote speech. The elephant urinated on the convention floor of the George R Brown Convention Center on Friday, drawing widespread attention and raising animal welfare concerns.

Organizers had warned attendees to keep the aisles clear in preparation for the "larger-than-life surprise." The incident became a focal point of media coverage and social media discussion during the convention.

cards.headline: Ticketmaster resolves confusion over Knicks game access
cards.teaser: A note on the Ticketmaster website caused panic among New York Knicks fans about potential lockout from an upcoming game.
cards.body:
Ticketmaster clarified that New York Knicks fans will not be locked out of an upcoming game after a confusing message on the ticketing website sparked backlash among New Yorkers. The note, which appeared when purchasing tickets, raised concerns about fan access to the game.

Ticketmaster moved quickly to address the situation and reassure ticket holders that they would be able to attend as planned.

cards.headline: Norway awaits verdict in crown princess's son rape trial
cards.teaser: Marius Borg Hiby will appear via video link for the verdict in his trial on 40 charges including four counts of rape.
cards.body:
Norway is bracing for the verdict in the rape trial of Marius Borg Høiby, the son of Crown Princess Mette-Marit. Høiby faces 40 charges, including four counts of rape. He will appear via video link for the verdict, which is coming almost three months after his trial concluded.

The case has drawn significant attention in Norway due to Høiby's connection to the royal family. The trial addressed multiple allegations across different incidents, and the verdict marks the end of legal proceedings that have been closely followed by Norwegian media and the public.

cards.headline: SpaceX IPO Creates 4,400 New Millionaires Among Employees
cards.teaser: The record-breaking SpaceX public offering has generated enough wealth on paper for thousands of employees to become millionaires, including some early workers who held relatively modest positions.
cards.body:
SpaceX's initial public offering has created approximately 4,400 millionaires among the company's employees who received stock compensation. The stock closed at $161 per share, up 19 percent from its offering price. A former SpaceX welder was among those who achieved millionaire status through the IPO.

The total paper wealth now held by SpaceX employees is sufficient to purchase every home in at least one Texas city. The IPO represents one of the largest wealth creation events for rank-and-file employees in recent corporate history. Elon Musk structured the offering to retain almost all voting power while allowing employees and outside investors to benefit from the company's valuation.

cards.headline: Elon Musk Takes SpaceX Public While Retaining Control
cards.teaser: Elon Musk is bringing SpaceX to the public markets through a record IPO while maintaining nearly complete control over the aerospace company.
cards.body:
Elon Musk has taken SpaceX public in what is being called the largest initial public offering ever. The company listed on the Nasdaq stock exchange with a valuation of $2.2 trillion while Musk maintained almost all decision-making power through a special share structure. When SpaceX first started, Musk said he gave the company "less than a 10% chance of succeeding at all."

The IPO has propelled Musk's personal wealth to $1.11 trillion according to the Bloomberg rich list, making him the world's first trillionaire. The offering allows public investors to buy shares in the space exploration company, though their influence over corporate direction remains limited.

cards.headline: Debate Intensifies Over How to Tax Artificial Intelligence
cards.teaser: Political figures across the spectrum say the public should benefit from AI wealth, but proposals for taxation vary widely.
cards.body:
Bernie Sanders, President Trump, and some AI companies have expressed support for ensuring the public benefits from AI-generated wealth. Despite this agreement on the basic principle, their proposed approaches differ significantly.

The various proposals for taxing AI reflect competing political and economic philosophies. While there is growing consensus that AI's benefits should extend beyond companies and investors, the specific mechanisms for redistribution remain contested. This debate unfolds as AI companies experience rapid growth and rising valuations.

cards.headline: Wages Decline as Asset Values Surge, Study Finds
cards.teaser: Workers are experiencing falling wages while wealth holders see surging asset values, creating economic discontent despite strong market performance.
cards.body:
A new analysis shows that while wealth has surged for those holding assets, wages are falling for workers facing higher prices and concerns about AI-driven job losses. The divergence comes as Elon Musk became the world's first trillionaire through his holdings in SpaceX and other companies.

The gap between wage earners and wealth holders helps explain why many Americans report economic dissatisfaction despite strong stock market performance and low unemployment rates. Workers face the dual pressures of reduced purchasing power from wage declines and anxiety about artificial intelligence potentially displacing jobs across multiple industries.

cards.headline: Amazon CEO reportedly flagged Anthropic model security issues before government action
cards.teaser: Andy Jassy may have been the source of concerns that led to a government crackdown on Anthropic models.
cards.body:
According to the Wall Street Journal, Amazon CEO Andy Jassy engaged in conversations with the White House regarding security concerns about Anthropic's models. This cybersecurity research from Amazon, combined with those discussions, reportedly contributed to an export control directive.

In response to the directive, Anthropic cut off worldwide access to two of its models—Fable 5 and Mythos 5—on Friday. Amazon holds a significant investment in Anthropic and integrates its AI technology across various services.

cards.headline: KPMG withdraws report on AI usage after apparent hallucinations
cards.teaser: The consulting firm pulled a report on artificial intelligence that appeared to contain AI-generated errors.
cards.body:
KPMG has withdrawn a report about AI usage after the document appeared to contain hallucinations, errors typically produced by AI systems that generate false or misleading information. The consulting firm's decision to pull the report highlights ongoing reliability issues with AI-generated content.

The incident adds to a growing list of cases where AI systems have produced inaccurate information, particularly when tasked with generating reports or summaries. KPMG has not detailed which specific errors appeared in the report or whether the firm used AI tools in creating the document.

cards.headline: NASA revises Artemis lunar lander plans
cards.teaser: The space agency is reshaping its approach to landing systems for the moon missions.
cards.body:
NASA has developed revised plans for the Artemis program's lunar lander systems. The changes come as the agency works toward the Artemis III mission, currently scheduled for 2027, which will return humans to the moon's surface.

The agency recently named crew members for the Artemis III mission, an all-male crew that has drawn criticism. NASA leadership has responded to concerns about the crew composition as the program moves forward with both technical preparations and crew assignments.

cards.headline: iOS 27 adds new features to Apple Wallet
cards.teaser: The update makes it easier to switch between payment cards and adds digital credential options.
cards.body:
Apple's iOS 27 update expands the Wallet app with six new features designed to improve both payment and credential management. Users can now switch between Apple Pay cards more easily, and a new "Create a Pass" feature lets them digitize physical credentials.

The update broadens Wallet's functionality beyond payment methods to support various types of identification and credentials. Improvements to transfer processes and expanded digital ID compatibility are also included in the update.

cards.headline: Fitbit Air launches as screenless fitness band
cards.teaser: The new wearable competes with Whoop and other tracker-focused devices.
cards.body:
Fitbit has released the Fitbit Air, a screenless fitness band that focuses on tracking rather than smartwatch features. The device competes directly with Whoop 5.0 and other wearables designed for continuous health monitoring without display interfaces.

Reviews of the device note that it includes an AI coaching feature that some users find excessive. The band is now available in India and other markets, offering an alternative to Fitbit's screen-equipped Pixel Watch lineup.

cards.headline: Samsung extends Galaxy S26 Ultra discounts in U.S.
cards.teaser: The flagship phone receives deeper price cuts months after its release.
cards.body:
Samsung has expanded discounts on the Galaxy S26 Ultra in the United States, with deals now available through multiple retailers. The 512GB model of the Galaxy S26 Plus is also receiving deeper price reductions than previously offered.

The discounts arrive just months after the S26 series launched earlier this year. Samsung is running the promotions as part of a mid-year sales push that extends through June 30, offering some of the lowest prices yet on its latest flagship devices.

hero.headline: Knicks one win away from first NBA title in 53 years
hero.body:
The New York Knicks are one victory away from capturing their first NBA championship since 1973 after completing the largest comeback in finals history on Wednesday night. The Knicks defeated the San Antonio Spurs 107-106 in Game 4, giving them a 3-1 series lead heading into Saturday's Game 5 in San Antonio.

The Knicks mounted an extraordinary rally from a 29-point deficit, a margin that seemed insurmountable for most of the evening. OG Anunoby delivered the game-winning basket with 1.2 seconds remaining, tipping in a missed three-pointer from Jalen Brunson to send the home crowd into celebration. The victory represents the greatest comeback the NBA finals has ever witnessed.

The Spurs dominated the early stages of the contest, racing to a 41-22 lead after the first quarter while making 11 of their first 16 attempts from beyond the arc. San Antonio extended their advantage to 76-49 by halftime, the largest half-time lead by a visiting team in NBA finals history. Their lead ballooned to 29 points before the Knicks began their unlikely recovery.

New York's turnaround began in the third quarter when they held San Antonio to just 14 points on 4-for-20 shooting. The Spurs managed only three points from Victor Wembanyama during this period. A decisive 28-9 run in the fourth quarter transformed the game entirely, with the Knicks converting defensive stops into fast-break opportunities that shifted momentum dramatically.

Brunson delivered the go-ahead basket with 1 minute 22 seconds remaining, putting New York up 105-104. After the Spurs retook the lead on free throws, Brunson's contested three-pointer at the buzzer missed, but Anunoby slipped through the defense for the winning tip-in.

Anunoby finished with 33 points and made seven of nine three-point attempts, both career playoff highs. Brunson added 36 points and seven assists in the victory. Jose Alvarado contributed eight crucial points off the bench during the fourth-quarter surge.

Wembanyama led the Spurs with 24 points and 13 rebounds, while Dylan Harper added 21 points. De'Aaron Fox and Devin Vassell each scored 18 for San Antonio, which was outscored 58-30 in the second half and managed just 3-for-17 shooting from three-point range after intermission.

The Knicks can secure the franchise's third championship in team history with a victory on Saturday. Only one team in NBA finals history, LeBron James's 2016 Cleveland Cavaliers, has recovered from a 3-1 series deficit to claim the title. The Spurs must replicate that feat to keep their championship hopes alive.

cards.headline: Golden Knights rule out center Karlsson for Game 6 of Stanley Cup Final
cards.teaser: Vegas will be without William Karlsson as Carolina looks to clinch the Cup at T-Mobile Arena.
cards.body:
The Vegas Golden Knights ruled out center William Karlsson for Game 6 of the Stanley Cup Final after he suffered an injury during Thursday's Game 5 loss.

The Carolina Hurricanes hold a 3-2 series lead and will attempt to clinch the Stanley Cup at T-Mobile Arena on Sunday. Karlsson's absence is a significant loss for Vegas as they face elimination and must win to force a Game 7.

cards.headline: UFC heavyweight title fight set as Pereira weighs in at 251 pounds
cards.teaser: Alex Pereira made weight for his heavyweight title bout against Ciryl Gane at the White House.
cards.body:
MMA star Alex Pereira weighed in at 251 pounds on Saturday, clearing him to compete in his heavyweight title fight against Ciryl Gane. The weigh-in occurred just over 24 hours before the bout.

The heavyweight championship fight takes place Sunday night at UFC Freedom 250, hosted at the White House.

cards.headline: Ticketmaster reverses course on NBA Finals ticket revocations
cards.teaser: The company clarified that no Game 5 tickets in San Antonio will be pulled after backlash from fans and officials.
cards.body:
Ticketmaster announced that no tickets to Game 5 of the NBA Finals in San Antonio will be revoked. The clarification came after the company faced criticism from Knicks fans and New York officials.

The reversal represents a victory for fans who had purchased tickets to the potential championship-clinching game. The company's initial policy had drawn significant backlash before Ticketmaster changed its stance on the matter.

cards.headline: Kentucky targets Michigan State's Batt for athletic director position
cards.teaser: The Wildcats have set their sights on J Batt to lead the athletic department.
cards.body:
Kentucky has targeted Michigan State athletic director J Batt to become the school's new athletic director, according to sources. Batt currently holds the athletic director position at Michigan State.

The move reflects Kentucky's effort to bring experienced leadership to its athletic department as it seeks to strengthen its standing in college athletics.

cards.headline: Former NFL defensive lineman Aldon Smith dies at 36
cards.teaser: Smith played six seasons in the league with three teams.
cards.body:
Aldon Smith, a defensive lineman who played six seasons in the NFL, died on Saturday at age 36. During his professional career, Smith competed for the San Francisco 49ers, Oakland Raiders, and Dallas Cowboys.

Smith's death marks the passing of a player who spent the majority of his career competing at football's highest level.

cards.headline: Golden Knights goalie dismisses fan chants about past legal case
cards.teaser: Carter Hart called Hurricanes fans' references to a 2024 sexual assault charge 'just noise.'
cards.body:
Vegas Golden Knights goalie Carter Hart dismissed fan chants from Carolina Hurricanes supporters about a 2024 sexual assault charge, calling them "just noise." Hart was acquitted of the charge and is focused on Game 6 of the Stanley Cup Final.

The Hurricanes lead the series 3-2 and will attempt to clinch the championship at T-Mobile Arena on Sunday. The Golden Knights will be without center William Karlsson, who was ruled out after suffering an injury in Game 5.

hero.headline: Gene Shalit, Film Critic Known for Mustache and Puns, Dies at 100
hero.body:
Gene Shalit, the longtime movie critic for NBC's Today show, has died at 100. The television personality became a recognizable figure in American households through his nearly four decades on the morning program, distinguished by his distinctive appearance and clever approach to film criticism.

Shalit joined Today in 1970 and became the show's arts editor in 1973. He remained with the program until his retirement in 2010. His physical appearance became iconic: he was known for his puffy hair and oversized handlebar mustache, features that made him instantly recognizable to viewers across the country.

Beyond his memorable look, Shalit developed a reputation as a middle-of-the-road critic with a talent for wordplay. His reviews frequently incorporated puns and wit, delivering his assessments of films with clever language that became his signature style. This combination of humor and intelligence set him apart from other critics of his era.

As a film critic on one of America's most-watched morning programs, Shalit reached mainstream audiences at a time when television was becoming an increasingly important outlet for cultural commentary. His position on Today gave him a platform that extended far beyond traditional print criticism, making him one of the most recognizable film critics in American media.

Shalit's long career spanned a significant portion of cinema history, from the classic Hollywood era through the modern age of streaming entertainment. During his decades on television, he reviewed countless films for morning audiences, helping shape how millions of Americans thought about movies.

His passing was reported by major news outlets including The New York Times, BBC, CNN, and The Washington Post. Al Roker, a longtime Today show personality, shared a tribute following the announcement of Shalit's death.

The moustachioed reviewer's retirement in 2010 marked the end of an era for a particular style of television film criticism. His presence on Today had made him a fixture in the daily routines of American viewers, and his influence on how film criticism was presented on television remained significant throughout his life.

Shalit's death represents the end of a distinctive era in morning television programming, when personalities like him could become household names through their regular appearances on network shows. His combination of distinctive appearance, intelligent commentary, and accessible humor made him a unique figure in the history of American media.

cards.headline: Kennedy Center Removes Donald Trump's Name From Building
cards.teaser: Court documents indicate that Donald Trump's name has been removed from the Kennedy Center performing arts venue after a court-ordered deadline passed.
cards.body:
Donald Trump's name has been removed from the Kennedy Center's facade in Washington DC. A federal judge set a Friday deadline for the removal, and after the venue missed it, work began in the early hours of Saturday. A judge rejected an emergency appeal to block the removal just hours before the deadline passed.

Crews used scaffolding to access the exterior of the performing arts venue. The words "The Donald J Trump and" were removed from the building's facade during the overnight work.

cards.headline: Seth Rogen Says He Has Not Spoken to James Franco in Years
cards.teaser: Seth Rogen told The New York Times that he has not spoken to James Franco in a long time and does not plan to work with him again.
cards.body:
Seth Rogen stated in a recent interview with The New York Times that he has not spoken with James Franco in a long time and has no plans to collaborate with him in the future. The actors previously worked together on multiple film projects.

When asked about his relationship with Franco following allegations of sexual misconduct against Franco, Rogen acknowledged the situation. The two actors had been frequent collaborators in Hollywood before their professional relationship ended.

cards.headline: Bruce Springsteen Apologizes for Declining Bono's Gap Commercial Request
cards.teaser: Bruce Springsteen expressed regret for refusing to license his song for a Gap commercial connected to Bono's AIDS foundation.
cards.body:
Bono addressed Bruce Springsteen's past refusal to license his song Girls in Their Summer Clothes for a Gap commercial supporting Bono's AIDS foundation (RED). The exchange occurred while Bono presented Springsteen with the Harry Belafonte Voices for Social Justice Award at the Tribeca Festival.

Springsteen told Bono he should have approved the request for the clothing brand partnership. The commercial would have supported the (RED) organization's work addressing AIDS.

cards.headline: Amy Adams Says She Rejected SNL Sketch to Protect Young Enchanted Fans
cards.teaser: Amy Adams told Seth Meyers that she turned down a graphic sketch idea from Andy Samberg while hosting Saturday Night Live in 2008.
cards.body:
During an appearance on Late Night With Seth Meyers, Amy Adams recalled turning down a sketch pitch from Andy Samberg when she hosted Saturday Night Live in 2008. She declined the "graphic" sketch idea because she was thinking of young viewers who had watched her in Disney's Enchanted.

The fairytale film had come out just four months before Adams hosted the show. She wanted to shield her younger fans from content she felt would be inappropriate for children.

cards.headline: Rosie O'Donnell Visits Daughter Chelsea in Prison
cards.teaser: Rosie O'Donnell shared details about visiting her daughter Chelsea in prison, calling it a significant day for both of them.
cards.body:
Rosie O'Donnell opened up about visiting her daughter Chelsea, 28, in prison. The comedian and television host shared a photo and thoughts about the reunion, describing it as a big day for both of them.

O'Donnell discussed the visit through poetry and shared her reflections with multiple media outlets. The visit comes after years of reported family difficulties between O'Donnell and her daughter.

cards.headline: Keke Palmer and Sean Evans Spotted Together in New York
cards.teaser: Keke Palmer and Sean Evans were seen on a date in New York City, fueling speculation about a potential relationship.
cards.body:
Keke Palmer and Sean Evans were photographed together in New York City during what appeared to be a date. The sighting has generated speculation about whether the two are dating.

Evans hosts the web series Hot Ones, where he interviews celebrities while they eat increasingly spicy chicken wings. Palmer is an actress and television personality who has appeared in numerous films and television shows.

hero.headline: Cruz endorses candidates opposing Trump picks in two governor races
hero.teaser: The Texas senator backed rivals to Trump-endorsed candidates in Georgia and South Carolina ahead of a possible 2028 presidential run.
hero.body:
Cruz Breaks With Trump on Key Endorsements as 2028 Looms

Texas Senator Ted Cruz is establishing his political independence from President Trump as he considers a potential 2028 presidential campaign, backing rivals to Trump-endorsed candidates in two significant Republican gubernatorial races.

Cruz announced this week that he was supporting Rick Jackson for Georgia governor and Alan Wilson in South Carolina's race for governor. Both candidates are competing against Trump-endorsed Republicans in upcoming runoffs.

Jackson, a wealthy health care executive, faces Trump-backed Lieutenant Governor Burt Jones in Georgia's June 16 runoff. Wilson, South Carolina's attorney general, is up against Trump-endorsed Lieutenant Governor Pamela Evette in a runoff scheduled for June 23.

The endorsements signal that Cruz is testing whether the Republican Party has room for a White House contender willing to break with a president who has maintained significant control over the party for the past decade. This represents a calculated political strategy as Cruz seeks to carve out his own political identity while Trump remains influential in Republican primary contests.

Cruz's moves come at a critical moment in the Republican Party. While Trump's endorsement remains the most sought-after prize in GOP politics, Cruz appears willing to challenge that dynamic by backing alternative candidates in high-profile races. His strategy suggests he believes there may be an opening for a 2028 candidate who can appeal to Republicans tired of Trump's dominance while still maintaining credibility within the party.

The timing of these endorsements is significant. With multiple Republican figures considering 2028 runs, Cruz is positioning himself as someone willing to make independent decisions rather than simply falling in line behind Trump. This approach carries risks, as Trump remains popular with many Republican primary voters and has shown willingness to target those who oppose his preferred candidates.

However, Cruz's endorsements also reflect broader trends within the Republican Party. Some Republicans have begun questioning whether Trump-endorsed candidates are the strongest choices in general election races, particularly in states where Trump remains unpopular. By backing Jackson and Wilson, Cruz is implicitly arguing that these candidates may be more competitive against Democratic opponents in November.

The Georgia and South Carolina races provide early tests of whether voters will follow Cruz's lead or stick with Trump's preferred candidates. Both runoffs will likely receive significant national attention as indicators of Trump's continued grip on Republican primary politics and whether any Republican figure can successfully challenge his influence.

As Cruz pursues his own political future, his willingness to openly oppose Trump's preferred candidates demonstrates that not all Republican leaders believe the party's future depends entirely on Trump's continued dominance. Whether this strategy proves politically viable will become clearer as the runoff elections approach.

cards.headline: US and Iran expected to sign peace framework Sunday
cards.teaser: President Trump said the US and Iran plan to sign an agreement aimed at ending their conflict and easing nuclear tensions.
cards.body:
President Trump announced on Saturday that the US and Iran plan to sign a peace agreement on Sunday. According to Trump's post on Truth Social, the deal would prevent Iran from obtaining nuclear weapons and reopen the Strait of Hormuz to international shipping.

However, Iran cast doubt on the timeline, stating that an exact signing date has not been decided and that it "will not be tomorrow." Democratic Rep. Seth Moulton of Massachusetts criticized the reported terms, calling the agreement a surrender document.

cards.headline: Trump nominates James McDonald as US Attorney for Manhattan
cards.teaser: The president tapped McDonald to replace Jay Clayton, who was nominated as director of national intelligence earlier this week.
cards.body:
President Trump announced Saturday that he plans to nominate James McDonald to serve as US Attorney for the Southern District of New York. The appointment fills a vacancy created when Jay Clayton, the previous US Attorney, was nominated as director of national intelligence.

The Southern District of New York is one of the most prominent federal prosecutor positions in the country, handling high-profile cases involving financial crimes, public corruption, and terrorism.

cards.headline: White House imposes export controls on Anthropic AI model after Amazon report
cards.teaser: The White House imposed export controls on Anthropic's Fable 5 AI model late Friday, ending public access to the advanced system just days after its release.
cards.body:
The White House imposed export controls on Anthropic's Fable 5 and Mythos 5 AI models following cybersecurity research from Amazon. According to the Wall Street Journal, Amazon CEO Andy Jassy engaged in conversations with White House officials that prompted the directive. Anthropic subsequently cut off public access to both models.

The sequence reveals how quickly the administration can act on industry concerns regarding AI capabilities. The involvement of Amazon, a major investor in Anthropic, underscores the complex dynamics within the AI sector as companies balance innovation with security considerations and government oversight.

cards.headline: Trump endorsement creates challenge for Hilton in California governor race
cards.teaser: The Republican nominee faces difficulty balancing the president's support with California voter sentiment where Trump is unpopular.
cards.body:
President Trump's recent voter fraud accusations in California have highlighted challenges facing gubernatorial nominee Steve Hilton as he campaigns with Trump's endorsement in a state where the president faces low approval ratings. Hilton, a British political adviser turned US politician, has promoted Trump's endorsement throughout his campaign as the most valuable backing in Republican politics.

The dynamic creates difficult terrain for Hilton as he attempts to appeal to California voters while maintaining his association with a president who polls poorly in the state. Trump's statements about voter fraud have drawn attention to how closely Hilton aligns himself with the president, a relationship that could help in Republican primaries but pose obstacles in a general election in California.

---

Note: The provided source material does not contain information about the Hilton campaign or California governor's race. The card text remains unchanged as instructed.

cards.headline: Burgum attributes gas price increases to state policies, not Iran tensions
cards.teaser: The Interior Secretary blamed Democratic state officials rather than Strait of Hormuz disruptions for regional variations in fuel costs.
cards.body:
Interior Secretary Doug Burgum said Friday that gas price variations across the country stem primarily from state policies and taxes rather than underlying market fundamentals related to the Iran conflict. Speaking to Fox News, Burgum shifted focus from the Strait of Hormuz turmoil to Democratic state leadership when addressing rising fuel costs.

Burgum pointed to several states' policy approaches as the main driver of regional gas price differences. The comments come as the administration faces questions about energy costs during ongoing tensions with Iran that have affected shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, a critical route for global oil transport. The secretary's framing places responsibility for high prices on state-level decisions rather than international disruptions.

cards.headline: Democrat criticizes reported Iran deal as surrender to Tehran
cards.teaser: Rep. Seth Moulton called the anticipated agreement a terrible deal after Trump announced plans to sign it Sunday.
cards.body:
President Trump announced on Saturday that the US and Iran plan to sign a peace framework on Sunday. The deal aims to prevent Iran from obtaining nuclear weapons and reopen the Strait of Hormuz to international shipping. However, Iran has cast doubt on the timing, saying an exact date has not been decided.

Democratic Rep. Seth Moulton of Massachusetts condemned the reported terms, characterizing the agreement as a surrender document. His criticism reflects broader Democratic concerns about the substance of the anticipated deal as details become public.
